messages:
Jamal: Heads up — Velvet tenant is hitting sustained p95 latency jumps starting ~2026-03-16 06:30 UTC on pool eu-dedicated-3. Users report intermittent 429s and model timeouts. I see SM util spikes on MIG slice 2 and elevated L3 eviction rates on that host.

InfraBot: [alert] eu-dedicated-3: token_latency_p95 +220% (06:31 UTC); affected_tenants=[velvet]; mig_slice_usage=[slice0:0.6,slice1:0.4,slice2:0.97,slice3:0.2]; autoscaler_state=stable

Sofia: Thanks Jamal. Can you paste the nv-smi and node-exporter snippet from the window? Also which MIG partitioning is in use on that node (1g/2g/4g etc)? Is Velvet colocated with any known heavy tenants right now?

Jamal: Quick paste from the host (redacted):
```
$ nvidia-smi dmon -s u -c 1
# gpu  pwr  temp  sm   mem  enc  dec
  0   315W  72C  98%  85%   0    0  (slice2 high SM)
```
And prometheus snippet:
```
node_gpu_cache_evictions_total{gpu_slice="2"} 12453
node_gpu_cache_evictions_total{gpu_slice="1"}  123
node_gpu_memory_bandwidth_bytes{gpu_slice="2"} 9.8e9
```
MIG config on that host is mixed: [1g.10gb, 2g.20gb, 4g.40gb, 7g.80gb], Velvet is on the 2g partition (slice2) but theres an internal analytics batch job on a co-located 4g slice starting ~06:28.

Alex: That pattern (high L3 eviction + uneven slice SM util) looks like cross-slice memory bandwidth bleed — small partition doing inference is losing KV cache locality when a big collocated job streams large tensor slices. To repro locally: start a synthetic bandwidth stream on a sibling slice and run a tight kv-cache-heavy infer loop on the 2g slice. Example (on a repro node):
```bash
# on sibling slice (simulate noisy neighbor)
python -c "import torch, time; a=torch.empty((10240,1024),device='cuda');
while True: a.a += torch.randn_like(a); time.sleep(0.01)" &
# on target slice (run small-batch inference probe)
python run_infer_probe.py --model small --batch 1 --steps 2000
```
If you see p95 jump and cache_evictions spike the same way, weve reproduced.

Sofia: Good repro plan. Short-term mitigations: 1) bump Velvet to a half-node reservation (no co-loc) or 2) temporarily move Velvet to a different host with identical MIG layout, or 3) apply an autoscaler policy to add another node and rebalance. Which option is lowest friction?

Jamal: We can try option 2 first (move tenant) — quicker than re-reserving. I ran a dry-run placement and found one free host with same MIG masks.

Karen: Ill coordinate the move. Oncall steps: drain-slice, remap-tenant, monitor for 30m. Jamal, can you provide the tenant id and the exact time window to check logs? Also set InfraBot to escalate to P1 if >3 tenants affected.

Jamal: Tenant id: velvet-prod-112. Check logs from 2026-03-16T06:25:00Z to 06:40:00Z. InfraBot: please tag if impact expands.

InfraBot: Acknowledged. Escalation rule updated for pool eu-dedicated-3: escalate_if_affected_tenants>=3 -> P1.

Alex: After move, let's capture perf counters (L2 miss, L3 eviction, DRAM bw) and also try a quick placement-change test: change Velvet to 4g partition temporarily and see if latency normalizes — that would confirm kvcache-bleed hypothesis.

Sofia: Agreed. Action items: Jamal=provide logs+confirm move; Karen=execute drain and remap; Alex=run perf-capture post-move. I'll follow up with a notes doc on root-cause once we have post-move metrics. :thumbsup:

Karen: Starting drain in 5m. Will post updates here when done.

Jamal: Thanks everyone. Ill attach the full prometheus scrape and the tenant callstack traces after the move.

Karen: Completed remap at 06:48 UTC. Initial 30m window looks good — p95 dropped back to baseline. Will leave monitoring for 2 hours and then close thread if stable.
